155	/****************************************************************************
156	 * Name: esp_interrupt
157	 *
158	 * Description:
159	 *   This is the common UART interrupt handler. It will be invoked when an
160	 *   interrupt is received on the 'irq'. It should call uart_xmitchars or
161	 *   uart_recvchars to perform the appropriate data transfers. The
162	 *   interrupt handling logic must be able to map the 'arg' to the
163	 *   appropriate uart_dev_s structure in order to call these functions.
164	 *
165	 ****************************************************************************/
166	
167	static int esp_interrupt(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
168	{
169	  struct uart_dev_s *dev = (struct uart_dev_s *)arg;
170	  uint32_t int_status = usb_serial_jtag_ll_get_intsts_mask();
171	
172	  /* Send buffer has room and can accept new data. */
173	
174	  if ((int_status & USB_SERIAL_JTAG_INTR_SERIAL_IN_EMPTY) != 0)
175	    {
176	      usb_serial_jtag_ll_clr_intsts_mask(
177	        USB_SERIAL_JTAG_INTR_SERIAL_IN_EMPTY);
178	      uart_xmitchars(dev);
179	    }
180	
181	  /* Data from the host are available to read. */
182	
183	  if ((int_status & USB_SERIAL_JTAG_INTR_SERIAL_OUT_RECV_PKT) != 0)
184	    {
185	      usb_serial_jtag_ll_clr_intsts_mask(
186	        USB_SERIAL_JTAG_INTR_SERIAL_OUT_RECV_PKT);
187	      uart_recvchars(dev);
188	    }
189	
190	  return OK;
191	}

267	 * Description:
268	 *   Configure the UART to operation in interrupt driven mode. This method
269	 *   is called when the serial port is opened. Normally, this is just after
270	 *   the setup() method is called, however, the serial console may
271	 *   operate in a non-interrupt driven mode during the boot phase.
272	 *
273	 *   RX and TX interrupts are not enabled by the attach method (unless
274	 *   the hardware supports multiple levels of interrupt enabling). The RX

276	 *   are called.
277	 *
278	 ****************************************************************************/
279	
280	static int esp_attach(struct uart_dev_s *dev)
281	{
282	  struct esp_priv_s *priv = dev->priv;
283	
284	  DEBUGASSERT(priv->cpuint == -ENOMEM);
285	
286	  USJ_RCC_ATOMIC()
287	    {
288	      usb_serial_jtag_ll_enable_bus_clock(true);
289	    }
290	
291	  usb_serial_jtag_ll_phy_set_defaults();
292	
293	  usb_serial_jtag_ll_ena_intr_mask(USB_SERIAL_JTAG_INTR_SERIAL_OUT_RECV_PKT);
294	
295	  /* Try to attach the IRQ to a CPU int */
296	
297	  priv->cpuint = esp_setup_irq(priv->source,
298	                               ESP_IRQ_PRIORITY_DEFAULT,
299	                               ESP_IRQ_TRIGGER_LEVEL,
300	                               esp_interrupt,
301	                               dev);
302	  if (priv->cpuint < 0)
303	    {
304	      return priv->cpuint;
305	    }
306	
307	  /* Attach and enable the IRQ */
308	
309	  if (priv->cpuint >= 0)

311	      up_enable_irq(priv->irq);
312	    }
313	  else
314	    {
315	      up_disable_irq(priv->irq);
316	    }

323	/****************************************************************************
324	 * Name: uart_interrupt
325	 *
326	 * Description:
327	 *   This is the UART interrupt handler. It will be invoked when an
328	 *   interrupt is received on the 'irq'. It should call uart_xmitchars or
329	 *   uart_recvchars to perform the appropriate data transfers. The
330	 *   interrupt handling logic must be able to map the 'irq' number into the
331	 *   appropriate uart_dev_s structure in order to call these functions.
332	 *
333	 * Input Parameters:
334	 *   irq           - IRQ associated to that interrupt.
335	 *   context       - Interrupt register state save info.
336	 *   arg           - A pointer to the argument provided when the interrupt
337	 *                   was registered.
338	 *
339	 * Returned Value:
340	 *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
341	 *
342	 ****************************************************************************/
343	
344	static int uart_handler(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
345	{
346	  uart_dev_t *dev = (uart_dev_t *)arg;
347	  struct esp_uart_s *priv = dev->priv;
348	  uint32_t tx_mask = UART_INTR_TXFIFO_EMPTY | UART_INTR_TX_DONE;
349	  uint32_t rx_mask = UART_INTR_RXFIFO_TOUT | UART_INTR_RXFIFO_FULL;
350	  uint32_t int_status = uart_hal_get_intsts_mask(priv->hal);
351	
352	#ifdef HAVE_RS485
353	  if ((int_status & UART_INTR_TX_BRK_IDLE) != 0 &&
354	      esp_txempty(dev))
355	    {
356	      uart_hal_clr_intsts_mask(priv->hal, UART_INTR_TX_BRK_IDLE);
357	      if (dev->xmit.tail == dev->xmit.head)
358	        {
359	          esp_gpiowrite(priv->rs485_dir_gpio,
360	                        !priv->rs485_dir_polarity);
361	        }
362	    }
363	#endif
364	
365	  /* Tx fifo empty interrupt or UART tx done int */
366	
367	  if ((int_status & tx_mask) != 0)
368	    {
369	      uart_xmitchars(dev);
370	      uart_hal_clr_intsts_mask(priv->hal, tx_mask);
371	    }
372	
373	  /* Rx fifo timeout interrupt or rx fifo full interrupt */
374	
375	  if ((int_status & rx_mask) != 0)
376	    {
377	      uart_recvchars(dev);
378	      uart_hal_clr_intsts_mask(priv->hal, rx_mask);
379	    }
380	
381	  return OK;
382	}

441	/****************************************************************************
442	 * Name: esp_setup
443	 *
444	 * Description:
445	 *   Configure the UART baud, bits, parity, fifos, etc. This method is
446	 *   called the first time that the serial port is opened.
447	 *   For the serial console, this will occur very early in initialization,
448	 *   for other serial ports this will occur when the port is first opened.
449	 *   This setup does not include attaching or enabling interrupts.
450	 *   That portion of the UART setup is performed when the attach() method
451	 *   is called.
452	 *
453	 * Input Parameters:
454	 *   dev           - Pointer to the serial driver struct.
455	 *
456	 * Returned Values:
457	 *   Zero (OK) is returned.
458	 *
459	 ****************************************************************************/
460	
461	static int esp_setup(uart_dev_t *dev)
462	{
463	  struct esp_uart_s *priv = dev->priv;
464	  soc_module_clk_t src_clk;
465	  uint32_t sclk_freq;
466	  bool success = false;
467	  irqstate_t flags;
468	
469	  /* Enable the UART Clock */
470	
471	  esp_lowputc_uart_module_enable(priv);
472	
473	  uart_hal_get_sclk(priv->hal, &src_clk);
474	
475	  esp_clk_tree_src_get_freq_hz(src_clk,
476	                               ESP_CLK_TREE_SRC_FREQ_PRECISION_CACHED,
477	                               &sclk_freq);
478	
479	  flags = enter_critical_section();
480	
481	  /* Initialize UART module */
482	#ifdef CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LP_UART
483	  if (priv->id >= LP_UART_NUM_0)
484	    {
485	      /* Enable LP UART bus clock */
486	
487	      LP_UART_SRC_CLK_ATOMIC()
488	        {
489	          lp_uart_ll_enable_bus_clock(0, true);
490	          lp_uart_ll_set_source_clk(priv->hal->dev, LP_UART_SCLK_DEFAULT);
491	          lp_uart_ll_sclk_enable(0);
492	        }
493	    }
494	#endif
495	
496	  uart_hal_init(priv->hal, priv->id);
497	
498	  uart_hal_set_mode(priv->hal, UART_MODE_UART);
499	
500	  if (priv->id < SOC_UART_HP_NUM)
501	    {
502	      esp_clk_tree_enable_src(UART_SCLK_XTAL, true);
503	      PERIPH_RCC_ATOMIC()
504	        {
505	          uart_hal_set_sclk(priv->hal, UART_SCLK_XTAL);
506	          success = uart_hal_set_baudrate(priv->hal, priv->baud, sclk_freq);
507	        }
508	    }
509	#ifdef CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LP_UART
510	  else
511	    {
512	      /* Override protocol parameters from the configuration */
513	
514	      if (!lp_uart_ll_set_baudrate(priv->hal->dev, priv->baud, sclk_freq))
515	        {
516	          /* Unachievable baud rate */
517	
518	          return ESP_FAIL;
519	        }
520	
521	      success = true;
522	    }
523	#endif
524	
525	  uart_hal_set_parity(priv->hal, priv->parity);
526	  set_data_length(priv);
527	  set_stop_length(priv);
528	  uart_hal_set_tx_idle_num(priv->hal, 0);
529	
530	  /* Define 0 as the threshold that means TX FIFO buffer is empty. */
531	
532	  uart_hal_set_txfifo_empty_thr(priv->hal, 10);
533	
534	  /* Define a threshold to trigger an RX FIFO FULL interrupt.
535	   * Define just one byte to read data immediately.
536	   */
537	
538	  uart_hal_set_rxfifo_full_thr(priv->hal, 120);
539	
540	#if defined(CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL) || \
541	    defined(CONFIG_SERIAL_OFLOWCONTROL)
542	  uart_hw_flowcontrol_t flow_ctrl = UART_HW_FLOWCTRL_DISABLE;
543	  uint32_t rx_thrs = 0;
544	
545	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL
546	  /* Configure the input flow control */
547	
548	  if (priv->iflow)
549	    {
550	      /* Enable input flow control and set the RX FIFO threshold
551	       * to assert the RTS line to half the RX FIFO buffer.
552	       * It will then save some space on the hardware fifo to
553	       * remaining bytes that may arrive after RTS be asserted
554	       * and before the transmitter stops sending data.
555	       */
556	
557	      flow_ctrl |= UART_HW_FLOWCTRL_RTS;
558	      rx_thrs = SOC_UART_FIFO_LEN / 2;
559	    }
560	#endif
561	
562	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_OFLOWCONTROL
563	  /* Configure the output flow control */
564	
565	  if (priv->oflow)
566	    {
567	      flow_ctrl |= UART_HW_FLOWCTRL_CTS;
568	    }
569	#endif
570	
571	  uart_hal_set_hw_flow_ctrl(priv->hal, flow_ctrl, rx_thrs);
572	#endif /* CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL || CONFIG_SERIAL_OFLOWCONTROL */
573	
574	#ifdef HAVE_RS485
575	
576	  /* Configure the idle time between transfers */
577	
578	  if (priv->rs485_dir_gpio != 0)
579	    {
580	      uart_hal_set_tx_idle_num(priv->hal, 1);
581	    }
582	  else
583	#endif
584	
585	  leave_critical_section(flags);
586	
587	  if (success == false)
588	    {
589	      return -EIO;
590	    }
591	
592	  /* Clear FIFOs */
593	
594	  uart_hal_rxfifo_rst(priv->hal);
595	  uart_hal_txfifo_rst(priv->hal);
596	
597	  return OK;
598	}

625	/****************************************************************************
626	 * Name: esp_attach
627	 *
628	 * Description:
629	 *   Configure the UART to operation in interrupt driven mode. This method
630	 *   is called when the serial port is opened. Normally, this is just after
631	 *   the setup() method is called, however, the serial console may
632	 *   operate in a non-interrupt driven mode during the boot phase.
633	 *
634	 *   RX and TX interrupts are not enabled when by the attach method (unless
635	 *   the hardware supports multiple levels of interrupt enabling). The RX
636	 *   and TX interrupts are not enabled until the txint() and rxint() methods
637	 *   are called.
638	 *
639	 * Input Parameters:
640	 *   dev           - Pointer to the serial driver struct.
641	 *
642	 * Returned Values:
643	 *   Zero (OK) is returned on success; a negated errno value is returned
644	 *   to indicate the nature of any failure.
645	 *
646	 ****************************************************************************/
647	
648	static int esp_attach(uart_dev_t *dev)
649	{
650	  struct esp_uart_s *priv = dev->priv;
651	  int ret;
652	  int source;
653	
654	  DEBUGASSERT(priv->cpuint == -ENOMEM);
655	
656	  /* Set up to receive peripheral interrupts */
657	
658	  source = uart_periph_signal[priv->id].irq;
659	
660	  priv->cpuint = esp_setup_irq(source, priv->int_pri,
661	                               ESP_IRQ_TRIGGER_LEVEL,
662	                               uart_handler,
663	                               dev);
664	
665	  /* Attach and enable the IRQ */
666	
667	  if (priv->cpuint >= 0)
668	    {
669	      up_enable_irq(ESP_SOURCE2IRQ(source));
670	      ret = OK;
671	    }
672	  else
673	    {
674	      up_disable_irq(ESP_SOURCE2IRQ(source));
675	      ret = -EINVAL;
676	    }
677	
678	  return ret;
679	}

681	/****************************************************************************
682	 * Name: esp_detach
683	 *
684	 * Description:
685	 *   Detach UART interrupts. This method is called when the serial port is
686	 *   closed normally just before the shutdown method is called. The
687	 *   exception is the serial console which is never shutdown.
688	 *
689	 * Input Parameters:
690	 *   dev           - Pointer to the serial driver struct.
691	 *
692	 * Returned Value:
693	 *   None.
694	 *
695	 ****************************************************************************/
696	
697	static void esp_detach(uart_dev_t *dev)
698	{
699	  struct esp_uart_s *priv = dev->priv;
700	  int source;
701	
702	  DEBUGASSERT(priv->cpuint != -ENOMEM);
703	
704	  source = uart_periph_signal[priv->id].irq;
705	
706	  /* Disable and detach the CPU interrupt */
707	
708	  up_disable_irq(ESP_SOURCE2IRQ(source));
709	
710	  /* Disassociate the peripheral interrupt from the CPU interrupt */
711	
712	  esp_teardown_irq(source, priv->cpuint);
713	  priv->cpuint = -ENOMEM;
714	}

716	/****************************************************************************
717	 * Name: esp_txint
718	 *
719	 * Description:
720	 *   Enable or disable TX interrupts.
721	 *
722	 * Input Parameters:
723	 *   dev           - Pointer to the serial driver struct.
724	 *   enable        - If true enables the TX interrupt, if false disables it.
725	 *
726	 * Returned Value:
727	 *   None.
728	 *
729	 ****************************************************************************/
730	
731	static void esp_txint(uart_dev_t *dev, bool enable)
732	{
733	  struct esp_uart_s *priv = dev->priv;
734	  uint32_t ints_mask = UART_INTR_TXFIFO_EMPTY | UART_INTR_TX_DONE;
735	
736	  if (enable)
737	    {
738	      /* After all bytes physically transmitted in the RS485 bus
739	       * the TX_BRK_IDLE will indicate we can disable the TX pin.

935	 * Name: esp_ioctl
936	 *
937	 * Description:
938	 *   All ioctl calls will be routed through this method.
939	 *   Here it's employed to implement the TERMIOS ioctls and TIOCSERGSTRUCT.
940	 *
941	 * Input Parameters:
942	 *   filep         - Pointer to a file structure instance.
943	 *   cmd           - The ioctl command.
944	 *   arg           - The argument of the ioctl cmd.
945	 *
946	 * Returned Value:
947	 *   Returns a non-negative number on success; a negated errno value is
948	 *   returned on any failure (see comments ioctl() for a list of appropriate
949	 *   errno values).
950	 *
951	 ****************************************************************************/
952	
953	static int esp_ioctl(struct file *filep, int cmd, unsigned long arg)
954	{
955	  /* Get access to the internal instance of the driver through the file
956	   * pointer.
957	   */
958	
959	#if defined(CONFIG_SERIAL_TERMIOS) || defined(CONFIG_SERIAL_TIOCSERGSTRUCT)
960	  struct inode *inode = filep->f_inode;
961	  uart_dev_t *dev     = inode->i_private;
962	#endif
963	  int ret = OK;
964	
965	  /* Run the requested ioctl command. */
966	
967	  switch (cmd)
968	    {
969	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_TIOCSERGSTRUCT
970	
971	    /* Get the internal driver data structure for debug purposes */
972	
973	    case TIOCSERGSTRUCT:
974	      {
975	         struct esp_uart_s *user = (struct esp_uart_s *)arg;
976	         if (user == NULL)
977	           {
978	             ret = -EINVAL;
979	           }
980	         else
981	           {
982	             memcpy(user, dev->priv, sizeof(struct esp_uart_s));
983	           }
984	       }
985	       break;
986	#endif
987	
988	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_TERMIOS
989	
990	    /* Fill a termios structure with the required information */
991	
992	    case TCGETS:
993	      {
994	        struct termios *termiosp = (struct termios *)arg;
995	        struct esp_uart_s *priv  = (struct esp_uart_s *)dev->priv;
996	        if (termiosp == NULL)
997	          {
998	            ret = -EINVAL;
999	            break;
1000	          }
1001	
1002	        /* Return parity (0 = no parity, 1 = odd parity, 2 = even parity) */
1003	
1004	        termiosp->c_cflag = ((priv->parity != 0) ? PARENB : 0) |
1005	                            ((priv->parity == 1) ? PARODD : 0);
1006	
1007	        /* Return stop bits */
1008	
1009	        termiosp->c_cflag |= (priv->stop_b2) ? CSTOPB : 0;
1010	
1011	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_OFLOWCONTROL
1012	        termiosp->c_cflag |= (priv->oflow) ? CCTS_OFLOW : 0;
1013	#endif
1014	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL
1015	        termiosp->c_cflag |= (priv->iflow) ? CRTS_IFLOW : 0;
1016	#endif
1017	
1018	        /* Set the baud rate in termiosp using the cfsetispeed interface */
1019	
1020	        cfsetispeed(termiosp, priv->baud);
1021	
1022	        /* Return number of bits */
1023	
1024	        switch (priv->bits)
1025	          {
1026	            case 5:
1027	              termiosp->c_cflag |= CS5;
1028	              break;
1029	
1030	            case 6:
1031	              termiosp->c_cflag |= CS6;
1032	              break;
1033	
1034	            case 7:
1035	              termiosp->c_cflag |= CS7;
1036	              break;
1037	
1038	            case 8:
1039	            default:
1040	              termiosp->c_cflag |= CS8;
1041	              break;
1042	          }
1043	      }
1044	      break;
1045	
1046	    case TCSETS:
1047	      {
1048	        struct termios *termiosp = (struct termios *)arg;
1049	        struct esp_uart_s *priv  = (struct esp_uart_s *)dev->priv;
1050	        uint32_t baud;
1051	        uint32_t current_int_sts;
1052	        uint8_t  parity;
1053	        uint8_t  bits;
1054	        uint8_t  stop2;
1055	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL
1056	        bool iflow;
1057	#endif
1058	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_OFLOWCONTROL
1059	        bool oflow;
1060	#endif
1061	
1062	        if (termiosp == NULL)
1063	          {
1064	            ret = -EINVAL;
1065	            break;
1066	          }
1067	
1068	        /* Get the target baud rate to change */
1069	
1070	        baud = cfgetispeed(termiosp);
1071	
1072	        /* Decode number of bits */
1073	
1074	        switch (termiosp->c_cflag & CSIZE)
1075	          {
1076	            case CS5:
1077	              bits = 5;
1078	              break;
1079	
1080	            case CS6:
1081	              bits = 6;
1082	              break;
1083	
1084	            case CS7:
1085	              bits = 7;
1086	              break;
1087	
1088	            case CS8:
1089	              bits = 8;
1090	              break;
1091	
1092	            default:
1093	              ret = -EINVAL;
1094	              break;
1095	          }
1096	
1097	        /* Decode parity */
1098	
1099	        if ((termiosp->c_cflag & PARENB) != 0)
1100	          {
1101	            parity = (termiosp->c_cflag & PARODD) ? 1 : 2;
1102	          }
1103	        else
1104	          {
1105	            parity = 0;
1106	          }
1107	
1108	        /* Decode stop bits */
1109	
1110	        stop2 = (termiosp->c_cflag & CSTOPB) ? 1 : 0;
1111	
1112	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL
1113	        iflow = (termiosp->c_cflag & CRTS_IFLOW) != 0;
1114	#endif
1115	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_OFLOWCONTROL
1116	        oflow = (termiosp->c_cflag & CCTS_OFLOW) != 0;
1117	#endif
1118	
1119	        /* Verify if all settings are valid before performing the changes */
1120	
1121	        if (ret == OK)
1122	          {
1123	            /* Fill the private struct fields */
1124	
1125	            priv->baud    = baud;
1126	            priv->parity  = parity;
1127	            priv->bits    = bits;
1128	            priv->stop_b2 = stop2;
1129	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL
1130	            priv->iflow   = iflow;
1131	#endif
1132	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_OFLOWCONTROL
1133	            priv->oflow   = oflow;
1134	#endif
1135	
1136	            /* Effect the changes immediately - note that we do not implement
1137	             * TCSADRAIN or TCSAFLUSH, only TCSANOW option.
1138	             * See nuttx/libs/libc/termios/lib_tcsetattr.c
1139	             */
1140	
1141	            esp_lowputc_disable_all_uart_int(priv, &current_int_sts);
1142	            ret = esp_setup(dev);
1143	
1144	            /* Restore the interrupt state */
1145	
1146	            esp_lowputc_restore_all_uart_int(priv, &current_int_sts);
1147	          }
1148	      }
1149	      break;
1150	#endif /* CONFIG_SERIAL_TERMIOS */
1151	
1152	    default:
1153	      ret = -ENOTTY;
1154	      break;
1155	    }
1156	
1157	  return ret;
1158	}

1160	/****************************************************************************
1161	 * Name: esp_rxflowcontrol
1162	 *
1163	 * Description:
1164	 *   Called when upper half RX buffer is full (or exceeds configured
1165	 *   watermark levels if CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL_WATERMARKS is defined).
1166	 *   Return true if UART activated RX flow control to block more incoming
1167	 *   data.
1168	 *   NOTE: Espressif chips have a hardware RX FIFO threshold mechanism to
1169	 *   control RTS line and to stop receiving data. This is very similar to the
1170	 *   concept behind upper watermark level. The hardware threshold is used
1171	 *   here to control the RTS line. When setting the threshold to zero, RTS
1172	 *   will immediately be asserted. If nbuffered = 0 or the lower watermark is
1173	 *   crossed and the serial driver decides to disable RX flow control, the
1174	 *   threshold will be changed to UART_RX_FLOW_THRHD_VALUE, which is almost
1175	 *   half the HW RX FIFO capacity. It keeps some space to keep the data
1176	 *   received between the RTS assertion and the stop by the sender.
1177	 *
1178	 * Input Parameters:
1179	 *   dev           - UART device instance
1180	 *   nbuffered     - the number of characters currently buffered
1181	 *                   (if CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL_WATERMARKS is
1182	 *                   not defined the value will be 0 for an empty buffer or
1183	 *                   the defined buffer size for a full buffer)
1184	 *   upper         - true indicates the upper watermark was crossed where
1185	 *                   false indicates the lower watermark has been crossed
1186	 *
1187	 * Returned Value:
1188	 *   true if RX flow control activated.
1189	 *
1190	 ****************************************************************************/
1191	
1192	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL
1193	static bool esp_rxflowcontrol(uart_dev_t *dev, unsigned int nbuffered,
1194	                              bool upper)
1195	{
1196	  bool ret = false;
1197	  struct esp_uart_s *priv = dev->priv;
1198	  uart_hw_flowcontrol_t flow_ctrl;
1199	
1200	  uart_hal_get_hw_flow_ctrl(priv->hal, &flow_ctrl);
1201	  if (priv->iflow)
1202	    {
1203	      flow_ctrl |= UART_HW_FLOWCTRL_RTS;
1204	      if (nbuffered == 0 || !upper)
1205	        {
1206	          /* Empty buffer, RTS should be de-asserted and logic in above
1207	           * layers should re-enable RX interrupt.
1208	           */
1209	
1210	          uart_hal_set_hw_flow_ctrl(priv->hal, flow_ctrl,
1211	                                    (uint8_t)(SOC_UART_FIFO_LEN / 2));
1212	          esp_rxint(dev, true);
1213	          ret = false;
1214	        }
1215	      else
1216	        {
1217	          /* If the RX buffer is not zero and watermarks are not enabled,
1218	           * then this function is called to announce RX buffer is full.
1219	           * The first thing it should do is to immediately assert RTS.
1220	           * Software RX FIFO is full, so besides asserting RTS, it's
1221	           * necessary to disable RX interrupts to prevent remaining bytes
1222	           * (that arrive after asserting RTS) to be pushed to the
1223	           * SW RX FIFO.
1224	           */
1225	
1226	          uart_hal_set_hw_flow_ctrl(priv->hal, flow_ctrl, 0);
1227	          esp_rxint(dev, false);
1228	          ret = true;
1229	        }
1230	    }
1231	
1232	  return ret;
1233	}

function cleanup()
{
  # keep the mapping but change to the link since:
  # 1.root can't access mount point created by normal user
  # 2.debugger could find the source code without manual setting
  fusermount -u ${MOUNTDIR}
  rmdir ${MOUNTDIR}
  ln -s ${ROOTDIR} ${MOUNTDIR}
}

function mount_unionfs()
{
  echo -e "Mount command line:"
  echo -e "  unionfs-fuse -o cow ${OUTDIR}=RW:${ROOTDIR}=RO ${MOUNTDIR}"

  rm -f ${MOUNTDIR}
  mkdir -p ${MOUNTDIR}
  unionfs-fuse -o cow ${OUTDIR}=RW:${ROOTDIR}=RO ${MOUNTDIR}
}


function build_board()
{
  echo -e "Build command line:"
  echo -e "  ${TOOLSDIR}/configure.sh -e $1"
  echo -e "  make -C ${NUTTXDIR} EXTRAFLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS" ${@:2}"
  echo -e "  make -C ${NUTTXDIR} savedefconfig"

  KCONFIG_ARGS="--enable-mconf --disable-nconf --disable-gconf --disable-qconf"
  if [ `uname` == "Darwin" ]; then
    KCONFIG_ARGS+=" --disable-shared --enable-static"
  fi

  if [ ! -f "${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends/bin/kconfig-conf" ] &&
     [ ! -x "$(command -v kconfig-conf)" ]; then
    pushd ${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends
    ./configure --prefix=${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends ${KCONFIG_ARGS} 1>/dev/null
    touch aclocal.m4 Makefile.in
    make install 1>/dev/null
    popd
  fi
  export PATH=${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends/bin:$PATH

  if ! ${TOOLSDIR}/configure.sh -e $1; then
    echo "Error: ############# config ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 1
  fi

  if [[ ${CUSTOM_COMPILER} == "tasking" ]]; then
    kconfig-tweak --file ${NUTTXDIR}/.config --enable CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING
  fi

  GHS_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_ARCH_TOOLCHAIN_GHS=y"
  TASKING_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING=y"
  if grep -qE "^(${GHS_OPTS_STRING}|${TASKING_OPTS_STRING})$" "${NUTTXDIR}/.config"; then
    echo "EXTRA_FLAGS are required to update the when using the GHS or Tasking toolchain."
    EXTRA_FLAGS=$(echo "$EXTRA_FLAGS" | sed 's/-Wno-cpp//' | xargs)
  fi

  if ! ${BEAR} make -C ${NUTTXDIR} EXTRAFLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS" ${@:2}; then
    echo "Error: ############# build ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 2
  else
    if [ -f "${COMPILE_COMMANDS}" ]; then
      cp ${COMPILE_COMMANDS} ${COMPILE_COMMANDS_BACKUP}
    fi
  fi

  if echo "${@:2}" | grep -q "distclean"; then
    if [ -f "${COMPILE_COMMANDS}" ]; then
      rm -rf ${COMPILE_COMMANDS}
    fi
    return;
  fi

  if ! make -C ${NUTTXDIR} savedefconfig; then
    echo "Error: ############# save ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 3
  fi

  if [ ! -d $1 ]; then
    cp ${NUTTXDIR}/defconfig ${ROOTDIR}/nuttx/boards/*/*/${1/[:|\/]//configs/}
  else
    if grep -q "#include" "$1/defconfig"; then
      echo "Note: skipping savedefconfig for debug defconfig."
    else
      cp ${NUTTXDIR}/defconfig $1
    fi
  fi
}

function build_board_cmake()
{
  # first check if the command target is `distclean`
  # cmake is built for out-of-tree, so delete the CMAKE_BINARY_DIR directory directly
  if echo "${@:2}" | grep -q "distclean"; then
    echo -e "Build target distclean:"
    echo -e "  there is no need to distclean in cmake, delete '${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}' directly"
    if [ -d "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}" ]; then
      rm -rf $CMAKE_BINARY_DIR
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # check parallelism
  j_arg=$(echo ${@:2} |grep -oP '\-j[0-9]+')
  # cmake verbose
  v_arg=""

  # remove the -Wno-cpp build option from ghs build options
  GHS_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_ARM_TOOLCHAIN_GHS=y"
  TASKING_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING=y"
  defconfig_path=$1/defconfig
  valid_defconfig_path=$(echo ${defconfig_path} | sed 's/^.\{3\}//')
  if grep -qE "^(${GHS_OPTS_STRING}|${TASKING_OPTS_STRING})$" "${valid_defconfig_path}"; then
    echo "EXTRA_FLAGS are required to update the when using the GHS toolchain."
    EXTRA_FLAGS=$(echo "$EXTRA_FLAGS" | sed 's/-Wno-cpp//' | xargs)
  fi
  export VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS"
  # let use lunch directily
  echo " lunch $1 ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} "
  lunch $1 ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
  echo
  # check if the command target is `Xconfig`
  for arg in "${@:2}"
  do
    if [[ $arg == *config ]]; then
      if ! m $arg; then
        echo "Error: #############  m $arg fail ##############"
        exit 2
      else
        return 0
      fi
    fi
    if [[ "$arg" =~ ^V=1$ ]]; then
      v_arg+="V=1"
    fi
  done
  # do cmake build
  if ! m $j_arg $v_arg; then
    echo "Error: ############# build ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 2
  fi
}


function setup_cmake_binary_dir()
{
  local boardconfig=$1
  if [ -d ${ROOTDIR}/${boardconfig} ]; then
    # parse path config
    config_name=$(basename "$boardconfig")
    board_name=$(basename $(dirname $(dirname "$boardconfig")))
  else
    # parse nuttx config pair
    config_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -s -d':' -f2`
    if [ -z "${config_name}" ]; then
      board_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d'/' -f1`
      config_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d'/' -f2`
    else
      board_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d':' -f1`
    fi
  fi
  CMAKE_BINARY_DIR+="/${board_name}_${config_name}"
}

  echo "Usage: $0 [-m] <board-name>:<config-name> [-e <extraflags>] [--cmake] [-b <cmake_binary_dir>] [--dis-ninja] [make options]"

  echo "Where:"
  echo "  -m: out of tree build. Or default in tree build without it."
  echo "  -e: pass extra c/c++ flags such as -Werror via make command line"
  echo "  --cmake: switch the build mode to CMake compilation."
  echo "  -b: set custom binary directory for CMake."
  echo "  --dis-ninja: disable CMake Ninja generator fo default."

    if [ "${CONFIGPATH:(-1)}" = "/" ]; then

    fi
    boarddir=`echo ${CONFIGPATH} | rev | cut -d'/' -f3 | rev`
    configdir=`echo ${CONFIGPATH} | rev | cut -d'/' -f1 | rev`
  else
    boarddir=${confparams[0]}
  fi

  OUTDIR=${ROOTDIR}/out/${boarddir}/${configdir}
  MOUNTDIR=${OUTDIR}/.unionfs
  NUTTXDIR=${MOUNTDIR}/nuttx

  trap cleanup EXIT
  mount_unionfs

else

  OUTDIR=${ROOTDIR}
  NUTTXDIR=${ROOTDIR}/nuttx

TOOLSDIR=${NUTTXDIR}/tools
board_config=$1

function cleanup()
{
  # keep the mapping but change to the link since:
  # 1.root can't access mount point created by normal user
  # 2.debugger could find the source code without manual setting
  fusermount -u ${MOUNTDIR}
  rmdir ${MOUNTDIR}
  ln -s ${ROOTDIR} ${MOUNTDIR}
}

function mount_unionfs()
{
  echo -e "Mount command line:"
  echo -e "  unionfs-fuse -o cow ${OUTDIR}=RW:${ROOTDIR}=RO ${MOUNTDIR}"

  rm -f ${MOUNTDIR}
  mkdir -p ${MOUNTDIR}
  unionfs-fuse -o cow ${OUTDIR}=RW:${ROOTDIR}=RO ${MOUNTDIR}
}


function build_board()
{
  echo -e "Build command line:"
  echo -e "  ${TOOLSDIR}/configure.sh -e $1"
  echo -e "  make -C ${NUTTXDIR} EXTRAFLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS" ${@:2}"
  echo -e "  make -C ${NUTTXDIR} savedefconfig"

  KCONFIG_ARGS="--enable-mconf --disable-nconf --disable-gconf --disable-qconf"
  if [ `uname` == "Darwin" ]; then
    KCONFIG_ARGS+=" --disable-shared --enable-static"
  fi

  if [ ! -f "${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends/bin/kconfig-conf" ] &&
     [ ! -x "$(command -v kconfig-conf)" ]; then
    pushd ${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends
    ./configure --prefix=${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends ${KCONFIG_ARGS} 1>/dev/null
    touch aclocal.m4 Makefile.in
    make install 1>/dev/null
    popd
  fi
  export PATH=${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends/bin:$PATH

  if ! ${TOOLSDIR}/configure.sh -e $1; then
    echo "Error: ############# config ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 1
  fi

  if [[ ${CUSTOM_COMPILER} == "tasking" ]]; then
    kconfig-tweak --file ${NUTTXDIR}/.config --enable CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING
  fi

  GHS_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_ARCH_TOOLCHAIN_GHS=y"
  TASKING_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING=y"
  if grep -qE "^(${GHS_OPTS_STRING}|${TASKING_OPTS_STRING})$" "${NUTTXDIR}/.config"; then
    echo "EXTRA_FLAGS are required to update the when using the GHS or Tasking toolchain."
    EXTRA_FLAGS=$(echo "$EXTRA_FLAGS" | sed 's/-Wno-cpp//' | xargs)
  fi

  if ! ${BEAR} make -C ${NUTTXDIR} EXTRAFLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS" ${@:2}; then
    echo "Error: ############# build ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 2
  else
    if [ -f "${COMPILE_COMMANDS}" ]; then
      cp ${COMPILE_COMMANDS} ${COMPILE_COMMANDS_BACKUP}
    fi
  fi

  if echo "${@:2}" | grep -q "distclean"; then
    if [ -f "${COMPILE_COMMANDS}" ]; then
      rm -rf ${COMPILE_COMMANDS}
    fi
    return;
  fi

  if ! make -C ${NUTTXDIR} savedefconfig; then
    echo "Error: ############# save ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 3
  fi

  if [ ! -d $1 ]; then
    cp ${NUTTXDIR}/defconfig ${ROOTDIR}/nuttx/boards/*/*/${1/[:|\/]//configs/}
  else
    if grep -q "#include" "$1/defconfig"; then
      echo "Note: skipping savedefconfig for debug defconfig."
    else
      cp ${NUTTXDIR}/defconfig $1
    fi
  fi
}

function build_board_cmake()
{
  # first check if the command target is `distclean`
  # cmake is built for out-of-tree, so delete the CMAKE_BINARY_DIR directory directly
  if echo "${@:2}" | grep -q "distclean"; then
    echo -e "Build target distclean:"
    echo -e "  there is no need to distclean in cmake, delete '${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}' directly"
    if [ -d "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}" ]; then
      rm -rf $CMAKE_BINARY_DIR
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # check parallelism
  j_arg=$(echo ${@:2} |grep -oP '\-j[0-9]+')
  # cmake verbose
  v_arg=""

  # remove the -Wno-cpp build option from ghs build options
  GHS_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_ARM_TOOLCHAIN_GHS=y"
  TASKING_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING=y"
  defconfig_path=$1/defconfig
  valid_defconfig_path=$(echo ${defconfig_path} | sed 's/^.\{3\}//')
  if grep -qE "^(${GHS_OPTS_STRING}|${TASKING_OPTS_STRING})$" "${valid_defconfig_path}"; then
    echo "EXTRA_FLAGS are required to update the when using the GHS toolchain."
    EXTRA_FLAGS=$(echo "$EXTRA_FLAGS" | sed 's/-Wno-cpp//' | xargs)
  fi
  export VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS"
  # let use lunch directily
  echo " lunch $1 ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} "
  lunch $1 ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
  echo
  # check if the command target is `Xconfig`
  for arg in "${@:2}"
  do
    if [[ $arg == *config ]]; then
      if ! m $arg; then
        echo "Error: #############  m $arg fail ##############"
        exit 2
      else
        return 0
      fi
    fi
    if [[ "$arg" =~ ^V=1$ ]]; then
      v_arg+="V=1"
    fi
  done
  # do cmake build
  if ! m $j_arg $v_arg; then
    echo "Error: ############# build ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 2
  fi
}


function setup_cmake_binary_dir()
{
  local boardconfig=$1
  if [ -d ${ROOTDIR}/${boardconfig} ]; then
    # parse path config
    config_name=$(basename "$boardconfig")
    board_name=$(basename $(dirname $(dirname "$boardconfig")))
  else
    # parse nuttx config pair
    config_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -s -d':' -f2`
    if [ -z "${config_name}" ]; then
      board_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d'/' -f1`
      config_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d'/' -f2`
    else
      board_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d':' -f1`
    fi
  fi
  CMAKE_BINARY_DIR+="/${board_name}_${config_name}"
}

if [ $# == 0 ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 [-m] <board-name>:<config-name> [-e <extraflags>] [--cmake] [-b <cmake_binary_dir>] [--dis-ninja] [make options]"
  echo ""
  echo "Where:"
  echo "  -m: out of tree build. Or default in tree build without it."
  echo "  -e: pass extra c/c++ flags such as -Werror via make command line"
  echo "  --cmake: switch the build mode to CMake compilation."
  echo "  -b: set custom binary directory for CMake."
  echo "  --dis-ninja: disable CMake Ninja generator fo default."
  echo "  -c: set custom toolchain."
  exit 1
fi

ROOTDIR=$(dirname $(readlink -f ${0}))
ROOTDIR=$(realpath ${ROOTDIR}/../..)

CONFIGPATH=$2

if [ $1 == "-m" ]; then
  # out of tree build
  confparams=(${CONFIGPATH//:/ })
  configdir=${confparams[1]}

  if [ -z "${configdir}" ]; then
    # handle cases where the end is a "/"
    if [ "${CONFIGPATH:(-1)}" = "/" ]; then
      CONFIGPATH=${CONFIGPATH:0:-1}
    fi
    boarddir=`echo ${CONFIGPATH} | rev | cut -d'/' -f3 | rev`
    configdir=`echo ${CONFIGPATH} | rev | cut -d'/' -f1 | rev`
  else
    boarddir=${confparams[0]}
  fi

  OUTDIR=${ROOTDIR}/out/${boarddir}/${configdir}
  MOUNTDIR=${OUTDIR}/.unionfs
  NUTTXDIR=${MOUNTDIR}/nuttx

  trap cleanup EXIT
  mount_unionfs
  shift
else
  # in tree build
  OUTDIR=${ROOTDIR}
  NUTTXDIR=${ROOTDIR}/nuttx
fi

TOOLSDIR=${NUTTXDIR}/tools
board_config=$1
shift

source ${ROOTDIR}/build/envsetup.sh

EXTRA_FLAGS="-Wno-cpp -Wno-deprecated-declarations"
while [[ "$1" == "-e" ]]; do
  shift
  EXTRA_FLAGS+=" $1"
  echo "extraflags: $EXTRA_FLAGS"
  shift
done

if [ "$1" == "--cmake" ]; then
  CMAKE_BINARY_DIR="cmake_out"
  CMAKE_GENERATOR="-GNinja"
  CMAKE_BUILD="cmake"
  setup_cmake_binary_dir $board_config
  shift
fi

if [ "$1" == "-b" ]; then
  shift
  CMAKE_BINARY_DIR="$1"
  echo "custom CMake binary dir: $CMAKE_BINARY_DIR"
  shift
fi

if [ "$1" == "--dis-ninja" ]; then
  CMAKE_GENERATOR=""
  shift
fi

if [ "$1" == "-c" ]; then
  shift
  CUSTOM_COMPILER="$1"
  echo "custom toolchain: $CUSTOM_COMPILER"
  shift
fi

# Determine the config path
if [ -d ${ROOTDIR}/${board_config} ]; then
  config_path="${ROOTDIR}/${board_config}"
else
  config_path="${board_config}"
fi

# Build with appropriate method
if [ -z "$CMAKE_BUILD" ]; then
  build_board ${config_path} $*
else
  build_board_cmake ${board_config} $*
fi

1	# NuttX RP2350
2	
3	NuttX RP2350 is a thin, reproducible integration repository for two RP2350
4	boards:
5	
6	- Adafruit Fruit Jam (`RP2350B`, PSRAM, ESP32-C6 ESP-Hosted networking)
7	- Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (`RP2350A`, no PSRAM, Infineon CYW43439 networking)
8	
9	The repository does not vendor Apache NuttX source trees.  `nuttx/` and
10	`apps/` are immutable submodule pins to `apache/nuttx` and
11	`apache/nuttx-apps`.  Project changes live in ordered patch stacks,
12	project-owned overlays, and eight independent profile defconfigs.
13	
14	FruitClaw remains the name of the optional operator application in the
15	`fruit-jam-full-fruitclaw` profile; it is no longer the project name.
16	
17	## Repository model
18	
19	```text
20	nuttx/ and apps/              clean pinned Apache submodules
21	patches/{nuttx,apps}/series   ordered modifications to upstream files
22	overlays/{nuttx,apps}/        project-owned boards, drivers, and apps
23	profiles/manifest.json        canonical eight-profile release matrix
24	profiles/<id>/defconfig       complete independent NuttX configurations
25	sources.lock.json             source, dependency, toolchain, and image pins
26	build/                        ignored per-profile staging trees
27	dist/                         ignored build and release output
28	```
29	
30	Builds never configure or patch the checked-out submodules.  Each profile is
31	materialized from the exact locked commits into `build/work/<profile>/`, then
32	patched, overlaid, configured, and built there.  A normal build therefore
33	leaves `git status` clean.  Parallel application compilation is retained, but
34	the completed `libapps.a` member order is canonicalized before the firmware
35	link so scheduling differences cannot change the UF2 bytes.
36	
37	## Release profiles
38	
39	| Profile | Board | Purpose |
40	| --- | --- | --- |
41	| `fruit-jam-minimal` | Fruit Jam | USB CDC NSH, Berry, vi, readline/history, Ctrl+C, I2C, watchdog; no network or PSRAM |
42	| `pico-2-w-minimal` | Pico 2 W | Same minimum contract on RP2350A |
43	| `fruit-jam-network` | Fruit Jam | Minimum plus ESP32-C6 ESP-Hosted `wlan0` and low-footprint network services |
44	| `pico-2-w-network` | Pico 2 W | Minimum plus Infineon CYW43439 `wlan0` and the same services |
45	| `fruit-jam-trmnl` | Fruit Jam | Working TRMNL client, ESP-Hosted, PSRAM, and 800x480 Y2 DVI output |
46	| `fruit-jam-doom` | Fruit Jam | Focused NXDoom image with PSRAM, DVI, SD, USB keyboard/mouse, and I2S audio |
47	| `fruit-jam-full` | Fruit Jam | Network plus the complete Fruit Jam driver and utility surface |
48	| `fruit-jam-full-fruitclaw` | Fruit Jam | Full image plus FruitClaw boot autostart |
49	
50	Network profiles include DHCP, DNS, `ifconfig`, `wapi`, `renew`, ping, wget,
51	NTP, netcat, telnet client/server, FTP client/server, and lightweight HTTPD.
52	Wi-Fi credentials are runtime data and must never be stored in defconfigs.
53	
54	### Fruit Jam network services
55	
56	The `fruit-jam-network` profile keeps Wi-Fi credentials on the SD card and
57	keeps them outside every remotely served directory.  After connecting Wi-Fi,
58	start the SD-backed services from NSH:
59	
60	```sh
61	source /mnt/sd0/wifi-up.nsh
62	useradd admin YOUR_PASSWORD  # first boot only
63	ftpd_start -4
64	webserver &
65	ifconfig
66	```
67	
68	Telnet starts with NSH and requires an account from the SD-backed
69	`/mnt/sd0/telnet.passwd`; provision it from the physical USB console, not in a
70	defconfig.  HTTP serves `/mnt/sd0/www` on port 80.  FTP uses the user `ftp`
71	with an empty password and confines that guest to the same `/mnt/sd0/www`
72	directory; `/mnt/sd0/wifi.conf` and the Telnet password database are not
73	reachable through either service.  Telnet itself is plaintext and is intended
74	only for a trusted LAN.  From a host on the same LAN, run the
75	repeatable service and SD transfer audit with the address printed by
76	`ifconfig`:
77	
78	```sh
79	NUTTX_TELNET_PASSWORD='YOUR_PASSWORD' \
80	  ./scripts/audit-network-services.py 192.168.2.7
81	```
82	
83	The Pico 2 W USB console baseline has been exercised on hardware.  Pico 2 W
84	Wi-Fi/services and NXDoom mouse/audio remain explicit hardware-validation
85	milestones; their presence in the build matrix is not a claim that those live
86	tests are complete.
87	
88	## Build
89	
90	Prerequisites are Git, Python 3, an Arm GNU toolchain, NuttX
91	`kconfig-frontends`, and `genromfs`.  Docker can provide the canonical release
92	environment.
93	
94	```sh
95	git clone --recurse-submodules \
96	  https://github.com/speccy88/NuttX-RP2350.git
97	cd NuttX-RP2350
98	./scripts/bootstrap.sh
99	./scripts/build-profile.sh fruit-jam-minimal
100	```
101	
102	Build every release profile:
103	
104	```sh
105	./scripts/build-all.sh
106	```
107	
108	The profile manifest is the sole release matrix.  Do not duplicate profile
109	lists in scripts or workflows.
110	
111	## Flash and connected testing
112	
113	Release images retain intentional recovery commands:
114	
115	- NSH `bootsel`
116	- 1200-baud USB CDC BOOTSEL touch
117	- host-driven `picotool reboot -u -f`
118	
119	Automatic watchdog-to-BOOTSEL recovery is forbidden in canonical release
120	defconfigs.  Release watchdog expiry performs a normal reset back into NuttX.
121	
122	```sh
123	./scripts/flash-profile.sh fruit-jam-minimal
124	./scripts/test-profile.sh fruit-jam-minimal
125	```
126	
127	Connected test runs use a generated development-only override:
128	
129	```sh
130	./scripts/build-profile.sh fruit-jam-minimal --dev-bootsel
131	```
132	
133	The override enables BOOTSEL recovery and a ten-minute BOOTSEL backstop only
134	inside the ignored staging tree.  Test tooling always attempts to return the
135	board to BOOTSEL before exiting and confirms that state with
136	`picotool info -a`.
137	
138	Fruit Jam SD-enabled profiles keep the proven SPI transport as their release
139	default while the four-bit PIO/DMA host is validated.  Build either transport
140	from the same profile without editing its defconfig:
141	
142	```sh
143	./scripts/build-profile.sh fruit-jam-full --dev-sd-mode spi
144	./scripts/build-profile.sh fruit-jam-full --dev-sd-mode pio
145	```
146	
147	Both images use `/dev/mmcsd0` and `/mnt/sd0`.  Cold-power-cycle the board and
148	card when changing transports; a soft reset may leave a card in SPI mode.
149	
150	## Releases
151	
152	Release tags use SemVer.  Until the hardware matrix is complete, publish only
153	prereleases such as `v0.1.0-rc.1`.
154	
155	Pushing a tag starts `.github/workflows/release.yml`; it performs two clean
156	digest-pinned container builds, compares each UF2 byte for byte, packages the
157	complete matrix, and creates the prerelease only if every asset is present.
158	
159	```sh
160	git tag v0.1.0-rc.1
161	git push origin v0.1.0-rc.1
162	```
163	
164	Every release is atomic: eight RP2350 UF2s, the matching ESP32-C6
165	ESP-Hosted-MCU binary, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and `build-manifest.json`.  A missing
166	profile fails the release; assets under an existing tag are never replaced.
167	
168	The manifest records both Apache pins, wrapper/tag SHA, profile and patch
169	hashes, toolchain and container identity, ESP-Hosted-MCU pin, sizes, and
170	SHA-256 values.
171	
172	## Updating Apache upstreams
173	
174	Pins never float during builds.  Test candidate commits explicitly:
175	
176	```sh
177	./scripts/update-upstreams.sh \
178	  --nuttx f27749b1b7339676bde10ec6852c9a7082fbaee3 \
179	  --apps c785d40af7b354a5ee312ad41e174e07875866da
180	```
181	
182	The update is accepted only if both ordered patch stacks apply, all profile
183	policies pass, and all eight isolated builds succeed.  Gitlinks and
184	`sources.lock.json` must move together in one reviewed change.
185	
186	## Project documentation
187	
188	- `docs/FRUITCLAW_WIFI_RELIABILITY.md` records FruitClaw/ESP-Hosted reliability work.
189	- `docs/FRUITCLAW_ISSUES.md` records known FruitClaw component issues.
190	- Board-specific documentation is installed through `overlays/nuttx/`.
191	- Historical FruitClaw tags and releases remain available after the repository rename.
192	
193	## License
194	
195	Project patches and overlays follow the license headers of their respective
196	Apache NuttX, Apache NuttX Apps, Berry, NXDoom, and component sources.  See
197	the source files and upstream projects for details.

## ESP-Hosted SDIO Transport Protocol Overview

**ESP-Hosted** is Espressif's solution for using ESP32 chips as Wi-Fi/BT co-processors (slaves) with a host processor (master). Key points:

### Architecture
- **ESP32-P4** → Can serve as the **host** (no built-in Wi-Fi, so it relies on a co-processor)
- **ESP32-C6** → Typically serves as the **slave** (has Wi-Fi 6 + BLE 5)
- **SDIO** is one of several transport options (others: SPI, UART, USB)

### NuttX Integration
- NuttX has been adding ESP-Hosted support, particularly for ESP32-P4 as host with ESP32-C6 as the Wi-Fi/BT slave over SDIO
- This involves:
  - SDIO transport layer driver
  - ESP-Hosted command/control protocol over SDIO
  - Integration with NuttX's networking stack

### Key Resources to Search For
1. **Espressif ESP-Hosted GitHub**: `github.com/espressif/esp-hosted`
2. **NuttX PRs/commits** related to ESP32-P4 + ESP-Hosted
